planting.note: Divide established clumps immediately after flowering or in early fall in moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; Trevi Fountain is a Terra Nova Nurseries hybrid noted for good powdery mildew resistance and better heat tolerance than many lungwort cultivars, useful for a Gulf South shade garden's humid summer.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Trevi Fountain is a vigorous lungwort hybrid with heavily silvered, green-margined foliage that stays attractive well into summer, resisting the powdery mildew that often disfigures lungwort leaves in humid weather better than many older cultivars. In early spring, clusters of funnel-shaped flowers open pink from the bud and mature to blue, creating an eye-catching bicolor display just as the foliage is emerging. It spreads at a moderate pace to form an increasingly effective groundcover under deciduous trees. Keep soil consistently moist, since lungworts decline quickly in dry shade, and divide congested clumps after flowering if the center starts to thin.

planting.note: Divide established clumps immediately after flowering or in early fall in moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; Majeste is a French-bred lungwort selection, introduced in the 1980s, prized for foliage that is almost solid silver rather than spotted.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Majeste is often cited as one of the finest silver-leaved lungworts, its broad leaves covered almost entirely in shimmering silver with only a thin green margin remaining, giving it a more uniformly bright appearance than the spotted patterning typical of most lungwort cultivars. Clusters of small, funnel-shaped flowers open pink and age to soft blue in early spring, appearing just as the striking foliage begins to unfurl. The dense clump makes an excellent, long-lasting groundcover once established, and the light-reflecting foliage is especially effective for brightening dark shade through summer. Keep soil consistently moist, since lungworts wilt and decline in dry shade, and divide after flowering if clumps become congested.

planting.note: Divide established clumps immediately after flowering or in early fall in moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; Silver Bouquet is a Terra Nova Nurseries introduction bred by Janet Egger, noted for good mildew resistance and heat tolerance that suits it to Southern shade gardens.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Silver Bouquet bears slender, narrow, almost entirely silver leaves that give it a more delicate, refined texture than broader-leaved lungwort cultivars, while still lighting up a dark shade bed effectively. Coral-pink, funnel-shaped flowers appear in early spring, opening before the foliage reaches full size and providing early-season color alongside daffodils and hellebores. It has been noted for good resistance to powdery mildew and better heat tolerance than many older lungwort selections, an advantage in a humid Gulf South summer. Keep soil consistently moist, since dry shade quickly causes lungworts to wilt and decline, and divide congested clumps after flowering.

planting.note: Divide established clumps immediately after flowering or in early fall in moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; High Contrast is a Terra Nova Nurseries selection, a seedling of 'Berries and Cream', bred for deer resistance and heavily ruffled, high-contrast foliage.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; High Contrast bears ruffled, dark green leaves heavily overlaid with silver, giving strong visual contrast that stands out even from a distance in a shaded bed. Pink flower buds open and age to blue in early spring, appearing alongside the emerging foliage for a two-toned floral display typical of the genus. It is noted for good deer resistance, useful where browsing pressure limits shade-garden plant choices. Keep soil consistently moist, since lungworts decline quickly in dry shade, and divide congested clumps after flowering to maintain vigor.

common_name: The Rocket Ligularia (Black-Stemmed Award-Winning Bog Perennial)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in constantly moist to boggy, humus-rich soil in partial shade with protection from afternoon sun; The Rocket is a Royal Horticultural Society Award of Garden Merit winner, though like all ligularias it struggles in zone 9 heat and needs a cool, sheltered, consistently damp site.

directions: Plant in constantly moist to boggy, humus-rich soil in partial shade with protection from afternoon sun and heat; The Rocket is a dramatic, architectural ligularia bearing bold, toothed, triangular leaves topped in mid to late summer by tall, striking spikes of small yellow flowers held on near-black stems that rise well above the foliage. It is one of the classic pond-edge and bog-garden perennials in cooler climates, holding a Royal Horticultural Society Award of Garden Merit for garden performance. Like all ligularias it wilts dramatically during midday heat, recovering overnight, which is normal behavior for the genus rather than disease; it performs best in climates with mild summers and struggles in zone 9 heat, so give it the coolest, most consistently damp spot available and mulch heavily to keep roots cool. Divide congested clumps in early spring every few years to maintain vigor.
